discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (2D materials, correlated electrons)
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that two graphene sheets twisted by a 'magic' angle near 1.1 degrees develop nearly flat electronic bands, where interactions overwhelm kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero and colleagues realised this experimentally, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. This work created an entirely new field, twistronics and moire quantum matter, in which the twist angle is a tunable knob for the electronic ground state. The platform has since revealed orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, Chern insulators and, in moire transition-metal dichalcogenides, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states. It unites materials, theory and spectroscopy, and hundreds of groups worldwide, including infrared and nano-optical studies, now use it. Rarely has a simple conceptual idea opened such a rich, programmable laboratory for strongly correlated and topological physics.
